title: The fire Christ came to cast and Lazarus dining with the risen Lord
english: Longing for our salvation, he has cried out elsewhere, saying, "Fire I came to cast upon the earth" (Luke 12:49). He is the one who wills mercy, the one who thirsts to be thirsted after, the one who swore by himself that he does "not wish the death of the sinner as much as his turning back and living" (Ezekiel 33:11). Fire the Savior came to cast upon the earth that he formed with his own hands and sanctified with the divine breath. Fire the Savior came to cast upon it, and to rekindle its free will, with which it had been honored by him from the beginning, and which the author of evil and deceit had taken away from it and enslaved in passions of dishonor. Fire the Savior came to cast upon it: that illuminating fire, the life-giving fire, the fire of the knowledge of God, the fire that consumes the thorns of impiety, that increases the seeds of the pious, that cuts away and uproots what is contrary to nature, and plants and cultivates the good things that are according to nature. He did this so that just as the human being was willingly led away with deceit and drew upon himself by his own choice the forewarned death resulting from disobedience, so again, sobering up from his stupor, he might recognize what is fitting and be brought near to God through confession and through turning toward him.

This divine and illuminating fire the Lord also kindled and set ablaze in Lazarus for the salvation of the Jews, providing them with a perception worthy of faith so that they might be saved. For signs are always given to the unbelieving, not to those who believe, as an occasion of salvation. For while they were contradicting and fighting against the truth, through his divinely powerful works he was showing himself to be God beyond dispute, as he himself says somewhere, "If you do not believe me, believe my works, so that you may know that the Father is in me and I am in the Father" (John 10:38). That is, as the radiance of the sun is in the sun, and as the sun is in its ray, without division and without variation, because of the consubstantial and self-empowered nature. And elsewhere, "The one who has seen me has seen the Father" (John 14:9), just as the tree is known in its fruit. And in another place, "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30), showing beyond all the equal honor and equal power. But let us return to the matter at hand.

"They made him a supper," John says, "and Lazarus was one of those reclining with him" (John 12:2). This is exceedingly magnificent for the true confirmation of the non-phantasmal resurrection of the one who had been saved. For so also the Lord himself, after his saving resurrection, showed himself to his genuine disciples, taking and eating before their eyes according to the law of human nature. For this reason also now the one who by the master's command had conquered the law of nature and death: this one dined with the master. The one who had risen rejoiced together with the one who raised him. The clay reclined with the fashioner. The one who had escaped the darkness celebrated with the light. The one leaping in bonds rejoiced with the one who looses the fettered in courage. The one who in the very reins of death, I mean the grave-clothes, having vigorously deceived Hades with a rushing sound, feasted together with the Lord who raised him.

But I will say to you: open for us, O divine head, John, your sacred tablets, for we are unable to grasp the boundless depth of the wonder. Yes, John says, Lazarus reclined with Jesus: the old and new man, whom Jesus called from corruption into life by a living and all-powerful word. The newly formed one reclined with him as with a nurse: with the one who by a command displayed a new birth of human beings. For it is the custom for the newborn children of the Jews to recline with the mothers who have given birth, filled with joy. "For when a woman is giving birth she has sorrow, because her hour has come; but when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the affliction, because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world" (John 16:21).

orientation: The preacher is expounding the supper at Bethany, explaining that the fire Christ came to cast on earth is the life-giving fire of the knowledge of God, and that Lazarus' presence at table proves his resurrection was real.
